title: The JABSOM exam cycle
lede: The schedule your work sits inside. Read this before you agree to an exam date.

blocks.text: None of this comes from ExamSoft. It is how OME runs exams, and it exists because an exam delivered on seventy-odd iPads has to be proofed, previewed on a real device, printed as a backup, and wrapped in proctor instructions before a student ever opens it.

items.detail: Questions written, ordered, categorized, and attached to the assessment. This is the handoff.
Staff preview the assessment on an iPad, come back to you on anything unclear, fix errors, and preview again. They print two hard copies and build the proctor PowerPoint.
Posting opens the download window. Students need the time to pull the exam onto their iPads.
Students cannot open the exam until then. Examplify locks the iPad for the duration.
Once answer files upload, the assessment overview shows you how the class did.

blocks.title: It is more than just clicking a button
blocks.text: That line is from the 2020 OME onboarding document and it has survived every revision since. The proofing steps run in sequence and they need the full 7 days. A late draft compresses proofing. It does not move the exam date.

blocks.title: Fix content problems before the download window opens
blocks.text: Once the assessment is posted and one student has downloaded it, you can no longer change questions or answer keys. After that point an error becomes a scoring adjustment.

items.label: Legacy Portal: Create and Preview a Practice Exam
items.note: Useful if you want to see what students see before the real thing.
